learningObjectives: Explain the physiological or methodological basis of Sampling Rate and Aliasing.
Apply Sampling Rate and Aliasing to technically valid clinical interpretation.
Identify artifacts, confounds and limits that could alter conclusions.
Communicate findings without exceeding the evidence or professional scope.

mechanismMap.label: Core concept
mechanismMap.detail: Sampling converts continuous voltage into discrete time points. Frequencies above the Nyquist limit can fold into lower frequencies unless filtered before digitisation.

mechanismMap.label: Mechanism
mechanismMap.detail: Sampling rate should comfortably exceed twice the highest frequency of interest. Anti-alias filtering and transparent acquisition settings are mandatory for reproducibility.

mechanismMap.label: Clinical integration
mechanismMap.detail: Incorrect sampling can distort fast activity, muscle artifact and high-frequency oscillations.

mechanismMap.label: Boundary condition
mechanismMap.detail: Upsampling later cannot recover information that was never captured.
